what: WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN. Baseline is data/verification/fix-batch-M5M7M8.json on release 9b449a41c865: protocol first-divergence 150 of 961, VOID 7, census 829 live / 829 probed.

scoreboard_called_in_advance.which_scoreboard: THE LAB, NOT THE POOL. The M6 fix moves an INSTRUMENT ADDRESS (MID_TGT), which is read by midEventDraw alone. It changes no game value, so no rollout, no self-play game and no seeded census probe can observe it. The probe is the scoreboard that should move; the pinned pool is expected to sit still.
scoreboard_called_in_advance.why_the_pool_may_not_improve: Before the fix the confusion self-hit damage roll was two INDEPENDENT dice (different addresses), which agree with probability 1/16. After the fix it is ONE SHARED die read in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: the authority takes Math.floor(u*16) because getConfusionDamage calls battle.randomizer directly and never enters the wrapped getDamage, while this engine takes damageRollIndex(u) = 15 - floor(u*16). Anti-correlated, so they now agree with probability 0. The direction of the pool change is therefore neutral-to-slightly-worse, and that is stated here rather than explained afterwards.

predictions.name: protocol first-divergence (diverged)
predictions.reason: No game value moved. The 10 confusion first-divergence causes in the baseline are already diverging and stay diverging. At most ~1 confusion self-hit in the pool currently agrees by luck and would now part; against that, every self-hit now draws a different u, which replays later turns and can move an unrelated first divergence by one or two either way.

predictions.name: VOID games (mid_void.void_games)
predictions.reason: The void check asks whether the addresses BOTH engines drew agree. The fix makes strictly more addresses shared and none fewer, so identity can only rise. A fall to 6 or 5 would be a real (small) improvement; a rise would mean the fix desynchronised something and is the failure mode to look for.
